question: What is the earliest recorded time frame for the return of ovulation following an abortion?
explanation: Ovulation can resume as early as eight to ten days after pregnancy termination, meaning unprotected intercourse during this early window can result in rapid repeat conception. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: Why is immediate post-abortion contraceptive counseling prioritized in clinical practice?

options.A: Patients are incapable of making decisions regarding family planning later
options.B: Hormonal methods interfere with uterine involution if delayed
options.C: Hospital policy mandates permanent sterilization after pregnancy loss
options.D: Fertility returns rapidly before the first normal menstrual cycle begins

explanation: Because ovulation precedes menses, waiting for a normal menstrual period before starting contraception exposes the patient to the risk of an unplanned pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: A client-centered approach to post-abortion family planning is best defined as which of the following?

options.A: Prioritizing hospital discharge speed over detailed method explanation
options.B: Strongly recommending long-acting methods to every single patient
options.C: Leaving the choice entirely to chance without clinical guidance
options.D: Facilitating informed choices aligned with the client's personal life goals

explanation: Client-centered care prioritizes the individual's unique preferences, values, and life circumstances rather than imposing a provider-driven agenda. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: Which assessment step is crucial before recommending a combined hormonal contraceptive to a post-abortion client?

options.A: Evaluating religious affiliation regarding family size
options.B: Measuring baseline pelvic floor muscle strength
options.C: Screening for cardiovascular risk factors and blood pressure
options.D: Confirming complete cessation of all uterine cramping

explanation: Combined hormonal contraceptives contain estrogen, which increases the risk of thromboembolism, making cardiovascular screening mandatory. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: What is the primary advantage of immediate post-abortion contraceptive initiation?

options.A: It eliminates the need for a separate return clinic visit
options.B: It completely stops all post-procedural uterine bleeding
options.C: It guarantees lifelong protection against unintended pregnancy
options.D: It removes all potential side effects associated with hormones

explanation: Providing contraception before the patient leaves reduces loss to follow-up and ensures immediate protection against subsequent unplanned pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: A patient presents with signs of an acute pelvic infection following an incomplete abortion. Which contraceptive management plan is most appropriate?

options.A: Prescribe high-dose oral estrogen pills to induce chemical sterilization
options.B: Insert a copper intrauterine device immediately to prevent further infection
options.C: Treat the infection and defer intrauterine device insertion until resolution
options.D: Refuse all contraceptive counseling until the patient is fully discharged

explanation: Placing an intrauterine device in the presence of an active pelvic infection risks worsening the condition and ascending pelvic inflammatory disease. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: Which of the following is classified as a long-acting reversible contraceptive method?
explanation: Subdermal implants and intrauterine devices are classified as LARC methods because they provide continuous, highly effective protection for years without requiring daily action. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: What factor contributes to a slightly higher rate of intrauterine device expulsion when inserted immediately after a second-trimester abortion?

options.A: Rapid degradation of copper wiring in tissue
options.B: Increased systemic blood pressure in the client
options.C: An enlarged and relaxed uterine cavity
options.D: Severe hormone imbalances unique to second trimester

explanation: After a second-trimester abortion, the uterus is larger and its walls are less toned, making it easier for an intrauterine device to be accidentally pushed out or expelled. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: What is a major clinical advantage of barrier methods compared to hormonal contraceptives?

options.B: Higher overall effectiveness in preventing pregnancy

explanation: Barrier methods such as condoms are unique in providing dual protection by simultaneously preventing both unintended pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: When can progestin-only injectable contraceptives be safely administered following an abortion?

options.A: Only if the client is over the age of thirty-five
options.B: Only after three normal menstrual cycles
options.C: Exclusively after surgical evacuation, never medical
options.D: Immediately on the day of the procedure

explanation: Progestin-only injectables have no estrogen-related cardiovascular contraindications and can be administered safely on the same day as abortion care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: Which of the following is a frequent community myth regarding modern contraceptive use?

options.A: Hormonal pills cure chronic infectious diseases
options.C: Barrier methods permanently alter menstrual flow
options.D: Intrauterine devices increase bone mineral density

explanation: A pervasive misconception is that using modern contraception leads to permanent sterility, a fear that nurses must proactively address during counseling. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: How should a nurse respond when a client expresses fear of weight gain from injectable contraceptives?

options.A: Force the client to accept an intrauterine device instead
options.B: Acknowledge the possibility, discuss lifestyle measures, and validate concerns
options.C: Dismiss the concern as unscientific nonsense and refuse further discussion
options.D: Guarantee that weight gain never happens to any user of the method

explanation: Validating client concerns and providing realistic information builds trust and helps clients manage potential side effects without abandoning contraception. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: What is an essential component of holistic post-abortion nursing documentation?

options.A: Documenting the exact financial cost of hospital supplies used
options.B: Recording the specific contraceptive method and patient education provided
options.C: Listing the names of all family members aware of the procedure
options.D: Detailing the precise political views of the client regarding abortion

explanation: Accurate clinical records must reflect the chosen contraceptive plan, details of counseling, and follow-up instructions to ensure continuity of care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: Why is psychological support considered a vital aspect of holistic post-abortion care?

options.A: Emotional distress directly inactivates hormonal contraceptive efficacy
options.B: Psychological counseling is legally required before any prescription can be written
options.C: Mental health evaluation replaces the need for physical pelvic examinations
options.D: Clients may experience a range of complex emotional responses following termination

explanation: Abortion experiences involve varied emotional landscapes; addressing psychological well-being ensures comprehensive, patient-centered healing. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)
